messages:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: elevated GPU preemptible reclaims in eu-west1-preemptible-pool. generation-service p95 latency spike -> 1.8s (baseline ~300ms). affected nodes: subset of az-a. traces show fallback to on-demand and cross-az routing.

aditya: seeing it in logs, lots of `InstancePreempted` events around 07:12. autoscaler churned and we got a burst of scheduling onto on-demand in other AZs.

maria: confirmed high enqueue time on serving queue, KV cache misses spiked. likely because KV caches lived on preempted nodes.

liam: quick check: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=preemptible -o wide` showed ~40% NotReady in az-a. sample output:
```
NAME                         STATUS     ROLES    AGE  VERSION
gpu-pre-az-a-5b   NotReady   <none>   12d  v1.28.2
gpu-pre-az-a-7f   NotReady   <none>   9d   v1.28.2
...
```

sophie: routing graph shows our fallback policy weights sent 70% to on-demand in eu-west1 and 30% cross-region eu-north1. cross-region added ~120ms.

aditya: mitigation idea: temporarily bias routing to local on-demand only (no cross-region) and spin up warm on-demand pool. downside: cost spike. thoughts?

maria: +1 for avoiding cross-region, that's adding latency spikes to critical paths. we should also reduce KV cache TTL to force rebuilds on new nodes more gracefully.

infra-oncall: executing toggle now: setting routing.fallback.crossRegionEnabled=false for generation-service. will also trigger on-demand warm-up (scale to +25 nodes).

ops_lead: call out cost impact: +25 on-demand GPUs ~ est $18k/day if sustained. but acceptable for 2-4 hours to stabilize.

monitoring-bot: action taken: routing.fallback.crossRegionEnabled=false at 07:18. autoscaler scale-up requested: +25 on-demand.

liam: after toggle, p95 dropped to ~520ms, p50 steady. KV cache rebuilds are happening but slower initial responses.

aditya: logging note: we should patch scheduler to prefer AZ capacity score over raw availability to avoid oscillating into flapping AZs. current logic picks highest capacity ignoring reclaim probability.

maria: short-term checklist (in thread):
- keep crossRegion toggle off until pool healthy
- drain remaining preemptible nodes in az-a gracefully (`kubectl cordon` + taint)
- reduce KV cache TTL to 30s temporarily
- add alert for cross-region-routing-surge

infra-oncall: starting drain now for nodes in az-a. command run: `kubectl cordon gpu-pre-az-a-* && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

monitoring-bot: New alert cleared: generation-service p95 back under 700ms (07:32). some background error logs (cache-miss bursts) still present.

ops_lead: longer-term proposals: diversify instance families in preemptible pool, keep a small warm on-demand standing buffer (3-5%), and add circuit breaker so we cap cross-region fallback to <10% of traffic to limit cascade.

aditya: agree. also add a short-horizon reclaim probability metric per AZ based on spot market signals (provider API). scheduler can weigh that in.

sophie: will open RFC for: 1) scheduler weight changes, 2) warm on-demand policy, 3) circuit-breaker for cross-region. priority: P0 for scheduler change.

maria: leaving notes for cost/eng: when toggling cross-region we should auto-annotate billing dashboard with the delta and tag these nodes for chargeback.

liam: postmortem data to collect: node reclaim events, kube-scheduler decisions, routing changes, end-to-end latency traces, KV cache miss timeline. I'll start a temp log export to s3 and link once ready.

infra-oncall: thanks team. reopening devcall @ 08:00 to walk through sequence and finalize roll-forward. :thumbsup:

monitoring-bot: incident closed (stabilized) at 07:40. escalation: none. follow-ups assigned in RFC #342.
